<coding_guidelines>
# AGENTS.md

How agents work in this repository. The rules are in [ai/RULES.md](ai/RULES.md) and win over
anything here; this file is the operational summary.

## What this is

droid-observatory: a Tauri 2 + Leptos (Rust) desktop app that shows a Factory Mission moving
through nine lanes, with validation, gate, agent attribution, waste and cost per sub-droid.
PRD: `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md`. Spec: `SPEC.md` (approved 2026-10-22; the mission plans from it).

Current state: no application code. The walking skeleton (core crate, canonical `Event`,
`observatory replay` over one captured session, an empty board that starts) is the first
thing the mission lands, before any milestone deepens its area.

## Setup, build, test

```sh
make doctor          # tool check with install hints
make hooks           # enable .githooks (once)
make check           # all light checks = mission-branch CI
make fmt             # rustfmt (no-op until Cargo.toml exists)
make lint            # clippy -D warnings
make test            # cargo test --workspace
make deny            # cargo-deny advisories, licences, bans
make replay-fixtures # observatory-cli replay over fixtures/streams/*.jsonl
make app-dev         # Tauri dev window (after the app exists)
```

Toolchain: `rust-toolchain.toml` (1.99.1, rustfmt, clippy, wasm32 target). Do not change it
without a decision file.

## Runtime limits (measured)

Measured 2026-10-22 on the owner's machine; source `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-validation-readiness.md`
(SPEC §5.8):

- At most 3 concurrent agent-browser validator sessions per `trunk serve` (1.34-1.54 GB RSS each,
  CPU negligible idle); use `--session <name>` per validator.
- `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone (1-min load 3.3 → 14.6 on 10 cores during the scratch run).
- All cargo builds serialize on the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` lock
  (`Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory`); expect waits, not failures.
- `trunk serve` and `cargo tauri dev` coexist only when exactly one trunk owns port 3141
  (`cargo tauri dev` starts its own); killing `cargo-tauri` alone orphans trunk and the app binary.
- Cold `trunk serve` 55.94 s, incremental 1.46-2.08 s, `cargo tauri dev` to running app 37.66 s.
- The Tauri window has no CDP endpoint; validators use the smoke check (process alive, `Running`
  log line, WebKit connections on 3141, System Events listing) plus the browser path on 3141.

## Interactive QA path

Until the app exists: `make check` is the only runnable target.
Once the skeleton lands, the path the validators follow is:

1. `make doctor` reports no missing required tools.
2. `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/<capture>.jsonl` prints lane
   events and ends with `unknown events: 0`.
3. `make app-dev` opens the window; open the same fixture (Replay); the nine lanes render
   and a card opens its Details view.
4. With the window open, start `droid exec --mission ...` in a terminal; the new session
   appears on the board (Attach) and each event shows within 1 s.

No login gate: the app watches and reads local session files and uses the GitHub token from the keychain or
`GITHUB_TOKEN` only for the gate lane.

## Layout and ownership

```text
crates/observatory-core   ingest, model, metrics, store, control (no UI deps)
crates/observatory-cli    headless replay/inspect over core
apps/observatory-app      Tauri 2 shell + Leptos UI
fixtures/streams          captured mission streams, named <YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.jsonl
docs/decisions            D-NNN-slug.md, one per decision; README.md is generated
docs/runbooks             recovery procedures: red gate, fix cycle, stall, hooks, release
reports/                  usage, waste, readiness; pasted from tools
build-log/                tool-call log written by .factory hooks
ai/                       PRD, rules, template, session logs
```

Crate and app paths are the contract the Makefile and CI probe for; keep them.

## Conventions

- Rust 2024 edition, `rustfmt.toml` and `clippy.toml` as committed. Warnings are errors.
- Naming: standard Rust (`snake_case` items and modules, `CamelCase` types, `SCREAMING_SNAKE`
  consts). Event kinds mirror the PRD §7 names in `snake_case`
  (`finding.blocking` → `FindingBlocking`). Lane and role enums use the PRD's words.
- Tests: unit tests in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` next to the code; integration tests in
  `crates/<crate>/tests/<topic>.rs`; fixture-driven tests read `fixtures/streams/`. Test
  functions read as sentences: `rework_window_closes_on_resolution()`.
- Tests before code (rule 1): commit the red test, then the code that turns it green.
- No magic numbers: every threshold lives in `config/observatory.example.toml` with a reason.
- Debt markers: `TODO(#123)` or `TODO(B-123)`; anything else fails `make check-todos`.
- Markdown: `.markdownlint-cli2.yaml`; links must resolve (`make check-links`).
- Files over 200 KB fail CI unless under `fixtures/streams/` or `build-log/`.

## Git

- Forward only (rule 12): never amend, reset, rebase, stash, or force-push. Fix with a new
  commit. `.factory/hooks/guard-git.sh` and `.githooks/pre-push` enforce this.
- Nothing reaches `main` except the mission's single pull request. `main` has a ruleset:
  PR required, `gate` check required, no force push, no bypass.
- Milestones live in worktrees and integrate into `mission/<name>`. Two worktrees never edit
  the same file (rule 13); shared files (`SPEC.md` §9–10, `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md`,
  `docs/decisions/README.md`) are written by the orchestrator at integration time.
- Commit subject under 72 characters; co-author trailer for agent commits:
  `Co-authored-by: factory-droid[bot] <138933559+factory-droid[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`.

## Decisions, backlog, logs

- A decision is one file: `docs/decisions/D-NNN-slug.md` with `**Date:**`, `**Status:**`,
  context, decision, alternatives, consequences. Run `make decisions-index` after adding one.
- Deferred work goes to the backlog (GitHub issues labelled `backlog`, indexed in `BACKLOG.md`)
  as `B-NNN` with a reason, not into TODOs (rule 14).
- Every session is logged under `ai/session/` with transcript links; every tool call is
  logged to `build-log/` by the PostToolUse hook. Do not disable the hooks.
- Usage and waste per milestone go to `reports/` pasted from the tool that produced them.

## Mission setup

Models per role (rule 19; `.factory/settings.json`; D-006):

| Role | Model |
|---|---|
| Orchestrator | `claude-fable-5.1` |
| Workers | `claude-sonnet-5-5` |
| Validators (scrutiny, user testing) | `claude-opus-5-5` |

Command: see README "Running it as a mission".
Reasoning effort: orchestrator `high`, workers `high`, validators `high` (SPEC §2).
A model change is a decision file.

The human answers only at milestone boundaries or when the stall flag is up (rule 15).
Deviations from the spec are proposed with reason and cost, and wait for approval (rule 9).

## Environment and secrets

See `.env.example`. Secrets come from the OS keychain (`droid-observatory/<name>` entries)
or the environment, never from the repository, the store, or logs. Raw session JSONL may
contain secrets: render read-only, never upload, never copy into the store.

- The GitHub token is a read-only fine-grained PAT; read check results via Actions runs
  (`/repos/{o}/{r}/actions/runs`) and commit statuses (`/repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{sha}/status`), not the
  Checks API (no Checks permission). Keychain items are generic passwords with service
  `droid-observatory/<name>` (see `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-dependency-readiness.md`).

Grafana Cloud OTLP (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*`) is the telemetry backend; export is off unless
`[telemetry].enabled = true`.

## Do not

- Add a dependency without `make deny` passing and a version verified on the day (rule 3).
- Write to `main`, rewrite history, or touch another worktree's files.
- Estimate a count, timing or token number: paste it from the tool (rule 7).
- Drop an unknown event: count it and show it (rule 18).
</coding_guidelines>

1. **Session file schema.** Droid session files carry no Droid version. The mapping version is

## 1. System overview and invariants

A Factory Mission writes one JSONL per agent session under `~/.factory/sessions/<cwd-slug>/`.
`observatory-core` turns those lines (and, later, a hosted JSON-RPC stream, local git and GitHub)
into canonical `Event`s on nine lanes, indexes them in SQLite by pointer, computes views and
metrics; `observatory-cli` exercises core headlessly; `observatory-app` (Tauri 2 shell + Leptos
CSR UI) renders the board. Attach (watch + tail) is the primary live mode; replay is attach at
end of file; host is the secondary path and the only one with a control channel (D-008).

Invariants every worker must keep (a violation is a blocking finding):

| # | Invariant | Where enforced |
|---|---|---|
| I1 | `observatory-core` is synchronous: no `tokio`, no `async fn` in its public API. tokio lives only in `apps/observatory-app/src-tauri`. | `cargo machete` + review; `Cargo.toml` of core has no async runtime |
| I2 | The UI holds no logic: card position, filters, scrubbing, tray count, details data, library entries are functions in `core::view`, unit-tested there. The Leptos crate only renders what the shell sends. | SPEC §6 "UI logic" |
| I3 | Raw lines are read-only and never copied into the store. The store keeps `path, byte_offset, byte_len`; the line is re-read on demand. `~/.factory/sessions/` is never written. | `store` DDL has no payload column; `JsonlSource` opens files read-only |
| I4 | Every `Event` carries `mapping_version` and a `SourcePtr`. | type system; test `every_event_carries_the_mapping_version()` |
| I5 | Unknown raw lines become `EventKind::Unknown { raw_type }`, are counted and shown (tray, CLI final line `unknown events: N`, exported counter), never dropped. | `mapping::map_record` is total: it always returns at least one `Event` |
| I6 | Thresholds and intervals come only from `Config` (`config/observatory.example.toml` is the contract); no literal in code. | `clippy.toml`; review |
| I7 | Secrets come only from the keychain (`droid-observatory/<name>`, account = login user) or, for the GitHub token only, `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Never in config, store, logs, telemetry, test fixtures. The `tracing` layer redacts (§12). | `secrets` module is the only reader |

| I9 | Core modules that the UI compiles to wasm (`model`, `mapping`, `view`, `metrics`, `config`) have no platform dependency; platform modules sit behind Cargo features (§2). | `trunk build` of the UI crate |

### 4.1 Source trait and RawRecord

```rust
pub struct RawRecord { pub ptr: SourcePtr, pub session_id: SessionId, pub bytes: Vec<u8> /* one line, no newline */ }
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)] #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum SourceKind { Jsonl, Rpc, Git, GitHub }

pub trait Source {
    fn kind(&self) -> SourceKind;
    /// Pull the next records. Returns an empty Vec when nothing new is available right now.
    /// Never blocks longer than one poll interval; never returns an error for "no data".
    fn next_batch(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<RawRecord>, IngestError>;
    /// True when every known file has been read to its current end (replay = attach that reached EOF, D-008).
    fn at_eof(&self) -> bool;
}
```

`[arch decision]` `next_batch` + `at_eof` replace SPEC §5.4's `poll`: the name says it pulls, and
`at_eof` is what makes replay and attach one code path (the CLI stops at `at_eof()`, the watcher keeps
calling). `IngestError` (thiserror): `Io { path, source }`, `FileMoved { path }`, `TooLarge { path, mb }`.

## 9. Metrics (`core::metrics`, M5)

Time states (PRD §10.1): `enum TimeState { Active, WaitingHuman(Question|Permission|Merge), WaitingValidation,
RetryFailure, IdleQueued, IdleUnscheduled }`. `pub fn partition(events_of_feature: &[Event], end: Timestamp)
-> Vec<Interval { from, to, state }>`, contiguous and non-overlapping
(`time_states_partition_every_instant_exactly_once()`). Active intervals `[arch decision]`: each event
with `duration` contributes `[at, at + duration]`; `duration` is set by the mapper as `tool_result.at -
tool_use.at` for tool calls and `assistant.at - previous_line.at` (same session) for model generation.
`ToolError`/`HookBlocked` intervals are `RetryFailure`; an open `QuestionAsked`/`PermissionRequested`/
green-but-unmerged gate with no active interval is `WaitingHuman`; `TaskDone` without a validator start is
`WaitingValidation`; a defined feature blocked by another's active interval is `IdleQueued`, else
`IdleUnscheduled`. The oracle (below) validates these rules.

Rework windows (`metrics::rework`): open/close pairs from PRD §10.2 (`FindingBlocking→ReworkResolved`,
`QaScenarioFailed→QaScenarioPassed` same scenario, `IntegrationConflict→IntegrationConflictResolved`,
`CheckFailed→CheckPassed` same check); overlapping windows on one feature merge; unresolved at mission end
reported with `closed_by = None`. Causes: `scrutiny`, `user_testing`, `integration`, `gate`.
Overhead (`metrics::overhead`): orchestrator intervals before the first `FeatureDefined`, replanning not
attributable, and compaction recovery; reported as its own line; `[metrics].overhead_apportionment =
"equal"` splits it and labels the output `apportioned`. Derived (`metrics::derived`): cycle (feature,
milestone, mission, per lane), waste by the 8 SPEC §5.6 causes, bottleneck (lane/role with highest
waiting + queued; lane with highest WIP/throughput), fix loops (count of `fix` cycles).

Cost (`metrics::cost`): tokens from `UsageReported` (sidecar `tokenUsage`); credits primary when
`factoryCredits` is present; otherwise `Σ tokens × per_m / 1e6` from `config/prices/<date>.toml`
(`[metrics].price_table`); every `Cost` carries `price_table: String` (the `effective` date)
(`cost_names_the_price_table_date()`). Budget meter: `[metrics].budget` or the launch `budget_usd`.
Model comparison (FR-M7): per role, per model, `cost_per_completed_feature` and
`first_pass_active_s_per_completed_feature`.

ingest thread records `Instant` when the mapped event reaches the store; the test asserts the maximum delta
< 1000 ms and prints `p50/p95/max` for the report (pasted, rule 7). It runs in `make test`; flakiness is
reported, not retried.

wasm test runner); the CLI has tests without a threshold; the shell is covered by the validators' smoke

## 3. Milestones

Seven milestones on the board of the build: the walking skeleton `S` first (rule 2), then
`M0`–`M5` in PRD §13 order. PRD §13 counts six; the seventh is the skeleton rule 2 requires, so
the PRD count is superseded here (rule 8). A milestone is integrated into the mission branch, never
shipped. The spec itself is not a milestone: it is approved before the mission starts.

**B-010 settled: skeleton before M0, and the capture is this mission.** Rule 2 wants the thinnest
end-to-end slice first; PRD §13 wants M0 to freeze the mapping before M1–M5 are planned in detail.
Both hold because the capture needs no extra mission: the moment the owner runs the §2 command, the
orchestrator's session JSONL is growing under `~/.factory/sessions/`, and the skeleton's workers
and validators add child sessions for every role. `S` replays a snapshot of that file through a
mapper that knows nothing yet (every line is `unknown.event`, counted). `M0` snapshots the same
sessions again at `S` integration, now with all four roles present, freezes it as the fixture,
and drives the unknown count to zero. The optional B-009 pre-capture is not needed; a small
sample-repo mission (PRD §13 M0) is the fallback only if role identification cannot be established
from this mission's own files.

**Common to every milestone.**

- Tests first (rule 1): each feature begins with a red test committed in the worktree; the
  scrutiny validator checks that the red run exists in the worker's log.
- Acceptance commands are the ones in §6 and `make check`; counts are pasted, not estimated.
- Exit needs: `make check` green on the mission branch after integration, `mission-checks` green
  on the push, zero blocking findings open, §9/§10 rows written, README/BACKLOG/decisions index
  updated (rule 16), `reports/usage/<m>.md` and `reports/readiness/<date>-<m>.json` added
  (B-015), and no `unknown.event` on the capture if the milestone adds a source (rule 18).
- Must not touch: `main`, another milestone's worktree, `rust-toolchain.toml` without a decision,
  the shared files (§2), the ruleset on `main`.
- Fixtures: `fixtures/streams/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.jsonl` is the orchestrator session; its child

## 5. Architecture

Each decision carries its reason. Numbers come from the PRD and `config/observatory.example.toml`
unless a reason says otherwise.

### 5.1 Crates and interfaces

| Crate / app | Responsibility | Public interface | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| `crates/observatory-core` | ingest, model, mapping, store, metrics, control, telemetry; **no UI dependency, sync, no tokio** | `Source` trait, `Event`, `Store`, `Metrics`, `Control`, `Config` | Testable from fixtures alone; every milestone's logic lives here so the UI can be swapped (PRD §12 go/no-go). |
| `crates/observatory-cli` | headless `replay`, `inspect`, `attach --watch`, `metrics --csv` over core | `observatory-cli <cmd>` | Rule 2: the first thing that works; rule 5: what CI runs; the validators' oracle for every milestone. |
| `apps/observatory-app` | Tauri 2 shell (`src-tauri`) + Leptos CSR UI (`src`) | Tauri commands and events, serde types imported from core | One language, no bindings drift (PRD §12). Commands are the only boundary the UI crosses, so a TypeScript UI could replace it without touching core. |

Tauri commands (M1 onward): `open_replay(path)`, `list_sessions()`, `attach(session_id)`,
`event_raw(ptr)`, `host_launch(cfg)`, `host_control(cmd)`, `metrics(scope)`, `gate(mission)`,
`merge(pr, target)`, `telemetry_status()`. Events from shell to UI: `events_appended(batch)`,
`session_discovered`, `stall_flag`, `gate_changed`. Batches flush every 100 ms (reason: well under
the 1 s requirement, avoids one render per line).

### 5.2 Canonical event and lane mapping

`Event`, `ReworkWindow`, `Lane`, `Role`, `EventKind` as in PRD appendix A; `EventKind` has one
variant per PRD §7 kind in `CamelCase` plus `Unknown { raw_type }`. `source: SourcePtr::Jsonl {
path, byte_offset, byte_len }` (appendix A has `path, byte_offset`; `byte_len` is added so a line
can be read without scanning for the newline) is the only thing the store keeps of a raw line
(PRD §11.2: the lane is a view). `mapping_version: MappingVersion` is a second addition to
appendix A: every `Event` names the mapper that produced it, so the first Droid upgrade shows as a
rising unknown-event count against a known version, never as a silently broken board (owner,
entry 23). Mapping is a module `mapping::v1` with a `MappingVersion`
selected from the Droid version in the session `.settings.json`; unknown Droid versions use the
latest mapping and raise a one-line warning (reason: an old capture must keep replaying, rule 18
covers the rest). A mapping version is frozen at M0 and never edited; a later Droid release gets
`mapping::v2` and its own fixture. The golden file `fixtures/streams/<capture>.events.json` is the
contract of a version.

### 5.3 Store schema

SQLite via `rusqlite` with the `bundled` feature (reason: core is sync, a desktop index needs no
async driver, and bundling removes the system-library dependency from the clean-clone rule).
File: `~/.droid-observatory/observatory.sqlite` (schema version table, migrations forward-only).

| Table | Columns (keys) | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `sessions` | `id`, `path`, `droid_version`, `tag`, `role`, `parent_id`, `mission_id`, `started_at`, `ended_at` | One row per JSONL file; `tag` confirmed in M0 |
| `events` | `id`, `session_id`, `mission_id`, `milestone_id`, `feature_id`, `lane`, `kind`, `raw_type`, `mapping_version`, `role`, `model`, `at`, `duration_ms`, `path`, `byte_offset`, `byte_len` | Pointer, never payload |
| `usage` | `event_id`, `input`, `output`, `cache_read`, `cache_write`, `credits` | From `usage.reported` |
| `missions`, `milestones`, `features` | ids, names, `defined_at`, `completed_at`, `state` | Board model |
| `rework_windows` | `feature_id`, `opened_by`, `closed_by`, `cause` | PRD §10.2 |
| `prs`, `checks`, `attestations`, `reviews` | GitHub ids, state, `observed_at`, `url` | Lane 8 |
| `human_actions` | `id`, `kind`, `target`, `at`, `payload_ptr` | Lane 7 |
| `prices` | `effective`, `model`, `class`, `per_m`, `source` | Loaded from the dated TOML |
| `mapping_versions` | `version`, `droid_version_range`, `frozen_at` | §5.2 |

Raw lines are read on demand from `path`+`byte_offset`; if the file moved, the UI says so and
shows the pointer (reason: never copy raw lines, PRD §11.2).

### 5.4 Ingest adapters behind traits

```rust
pub trait Source { fn poll(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<RawRecord>>; fn kind(&self) -> SourceKind; }
pub trait Forge  { fn pr(&self, branch: &str, target: &str) -> Result<Option<Pr>>;
                   fn checks(&self, pr: &Pr) -> Result<Vec<Check>>; fn policy(&self, target: &str) -> Result<MergePolicy>;
                   fn merge(&self, pr: &Pr, method: MergeMethod) -> Result<Merged>; /* attestations, reviews */ }
```

`JsonlSource` (attach; replay = the same source at end of file with a clock the scrubber drives),
`RpcSource` (host, M2), `GitSource` (M4), `GitHubSource: Forge` (M4). Reason: one adapter for
attach and replay removes a whole class of "works in replay, not live" bugs (D-008); the `Forge`
trait is the seam for other forges later (PRD §5 non-goal, §11.2).

## 6. Tests

Fixtures are captured streams, named and dated (§3). Local = `make check` in a worktree; MB = the
`mission-checks` aggregate on `mission/**`; PR = the `gate` aggregate on the final pull request.

| Suite | Covers | Where | Command |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unit (`#[cfg(test)]` next to code) | model, mapping helpers, time-state engine, windows, cost, label allow-list | local, MB, PR | `cargo test --workspace --all-features` |
| Fixture replay (`crates/observatory-core/tests/replay_*.rs`, `mapping.rs`) | each fixture → golden lane events, `unknown events: 0` on frozen captures | local, MB, PR | `make replay-fixtures`; `cargo test -p observatory-core --test mapping` |
| Attach latency (`tests/attach_latency.rs`) | harness appends a fixture line by line; event visible to the store within 1 s | local, MB, PR | `cargo test -p observatory-core --test attach_latency` |
| CLI (`crates/observatory-cli/tests/cli.rs`) | exit codes, `unknown events: N` line, `inspect` prints the exact raw line | local, MB, PR | `cargo test -p observatory-cli` |
| Metrics oracle (`tests/oracle.rs`, M5) | engine output vs `reports/reference/*.csv` within tolerance | local, MB, PR | `cargo test -p observatory-core --test oracle` |
| Telemetry budget (M5) | worst-case series count = 182 < 200; labels outside the set rejected | local, MB, PR | part of unit |
| UI logic | view-model functions (card position, filters, scrubber) live in core and are unit-tested there; the Leptos layer holds no logic worth a wasm test runner (reason: `wasm-bindgen-test` adds a toolchain step for little coverage) | local, MB, PR | part of unit |
| Interactive QA (validators) | board, Details, tray, filters, scrubber in the **browser host** `trunk serve --port 3141` with the fixture opened through the file picker; attach, host, controls and gate in the **Tauri window** (`make app-dev`) with screenshots and the CLI as oracle | per milestone, by the user-testing validator | `make app-dev`; `trunk serve --port 3141` |
| Coverage (B-005) | `observatory-core` lines | S: reported; **M0 onward: fail under 80 %**; MB and PR | `cargo llvm-cov -p observatory-core --fail-under-lines 80` |

**B-005 settled: 80 % lines on `observatory-core`.** Reason: core holds every piece of logic that
can be wrong silently (mapping, time states, cost), so it is where coverage buys correctness;
IO adapters that need a live `droid` or GitHub are in core too and cannot all be exercised in CI,
which is the 20 % of room. The CLI is thin and covered by its own tests without a threshold; the
UI crate is excluded (wasm target, no logic). Enforced from M0 integration because S has too little
code for a percentage to mean anything. Raising it is a backlog item with a reason, lowering it is
a decision file.

## 7. CI

Two workflows, one required check (D-003). Measured per run; the wall time of the aggregate is
pasted into `reports/ci/<date>-<milestone>.md` at integration (rule 11).

**Mission branch** (`mission-branch.yml`, on push and PR to `mission/**`; aggregate
`mission-checks`; budget 3 min warm): markdownlint, lychee, actionlint, file size, debt markers,
decisions index, gitleaks, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings`, `cargo test`,
`make replay-fixtures`, `cargo deny check`, plus from S: **`cargo machete`** (B-014) and
**`cargo llvm-cov` with the §6 threshold** (B-005). Independent jobs in parallel with the
rust-cache. Gates integration: the orchestrator waits for green before the next milestone. If the
warm time exceeds 3 min after the coverage job joins, coverage moves to the final PR only, by
decision file.

**B-014 settled: `cargo-machete`, not `cargo-udeps`.** Reason: machete runs on the stable toolchain
in seconds; udeps needs nightly, which is a second toolchain to pin and cache for a check that
finds a strict superset only in edge cases. Revisit if machete misses a real unused dependency.

**Demo gate** (`demo-gate.yml`, M4, on `pull_request` to `demo/base`): one job that fails when the
label `demo:red` is present. Required by the `demo-gate` ruleset on `demo/base` only. Never touches
`main`.

**Final pull request** (`gate.yml`, on PR to `main`; aggregate `gate`, the only check the `main`
ruleset requires): everything above plus Semgrep (SARIF to code scanning), Trivy filesystem scan of
the repository (vuln, misconfig, secret; HIGH and CRITICAL; `Cargo.lock` is what makes the vuln
scan meaningful), Checkov on the workflows, SBOM (`syft`), the macOS Tauri bundle (`bundle.yml`)
with build provenance (`attest-build-provenance`) and cosign signatures, Trivy results and SBOM
attached as artifacts. It never deploys. `release.yml` on `v*` tags pushed by the human to a
commit on `main` reuses `bundle.yml` and, from S onward, checks the workspace version against the
tag (B-016, wired in S; D-009).

## 8. Deliverables

Grown at every integration, never written at the end (rule 16).

- **README.md**: what it is, the clean-clone commands (`make doctor`, `make check`, replay,
  `make app-dev`), the mission command of §2, the gate, the demo branch pair, honest time and
  usage per milestone (rule 10, from `reports/usage/`), what was left out with the reason.
- **docs/decisions/**: one file per decision, `make decisions-index` regenerates the README. The
  mission writes at least: mapping v1 and the `--tag`/child-session findings (M0), coverage
  component and threshold (S), machete (S), series allocation (M5 or earlier), demo branch pair
  superseding the private repo (M4), hybrid backlog (S), any model or effort change (rule 19), and
  the M1 go/no-go outcome.
- **BACKLOG.md and the hybrid backlog** (entry 19, mission-driven): at S integration the
  orchestrator creates GitHub issues labelled `backlog` from the open B-items of this spec, adds
  `scripts/gen-backlog.sh` that regenerates `BACKLOG.md` from the issues at every integration, and
  writes the decision file. Items the spec closed (B-005, B-007, B-010, B-014, B-017) are marked
  done with this spec as the reason. **Rule 14 wording** proposed for owner approval with this
  spec (RULES.md is the owner's): "everything else goes to the backlog (GitHub issues labelled
  `backlog`, indexed in `BACKLOG.md`) with its reason". Until approved, `BACKLOG.md` stays the
  source and no issue is created.
- **build-log/**: one JSON line per tool call per session, written by the PostToolUse hook,
  committed with each integration (exempt from the 200 KB limit).
- **ai/session/**: one entry per interaction with transcript links; the mission appends to
  `ai/session/2026-10-22-session.md` (or a dated successor) at every boundary.
- **reports/**: `usage/<m>.md` (tokens, credits, USD-eq per role and model, pasted),
  `waste/<m>.md` (from M5 onward, computed by the observatory on its own capture),
  `readiness/<date>-<m>.json` (B-015, every integration), `ci/<date>-<m>.md` (aggregate wall time),
  `reference/` (the owner's spreadsheet, B-008).
- **Spec PR** (before the mission): this file, the model-id corrections already in the working
  tree (entry 21), the three reasoning-effort keys in `.factory/settings.json`
  (`missionOrchestratorReasoningEffort = "high"`, `workerReasoningEffort = "high"`,
  `validationWorkerReasoningEffort = "high"`), session log entries 20–23, the PRD §13 M4 row and

## 7. Lanes

The board has nine lanes. Lanes 1–6 are fed by the mission stream, 7–8 by GitHub and human actions, 9 by session metadata. Each event carries `session_id`, `role`, `model`, `timestamp`, `duration`, and a pointer to its raw JSONL line.

| # | Lane | What it holds | Source | Event kinds |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Intent** | Mission prompt, spec, acceptance criteria; later human re-prompts | stream (user ↔ orchestrator), mission file | `intent.created`, `intent.amended`, `question.asked` (orchestrator → human), `intent.answered`, `spec.versioned` |
| 2 | **Orchestrator** | Plan, feature breakdown, milestones, task assignment, replans | stream (orchestrator session) | `plan.created`, `feature.defined`, `milestone.defined`, `task.assigned`, `task.skipped`, `plan.revised`, `escalation.raised`, `milestone.completed`, `mission.paused`, `mission.resumed`, `mission.completed`, `context.compacted` |
| 3 | **Workers** | One sub-lane per worker (or per feature when the mission names them) | stream (worker child sessions) | `subagent.spawned`, `task.started`, `file.touched`, `tests.run`, `commit.created`, `task.done`, `subagent.finished`, `tool.error`, `permission.requested`, `permission.granted`, `permission.denied`, `hook.blocked`, `usage.reported`, `model.changed` |
| 4 | **Validators, scrutiny** | Review findings, blocking vs non-blocking, re-work requested and resolved | stream (scrutiny validator sessions) | `finding.blocking`, `finding.non_blocking`, `rework.requested`, `rework.resolved`, `scrutiny.passed` |
| 5 | **Validators, user testing** | QA runs against the built thing, scenario results | stream (user-testing validator sessions) | `qa.scenario.passed`, `qa.scenario.failed`, `qa.evidence` (screenshot, video) |
| 6 | **Integration** | Worktree merges into `mission/<name>`, conflicts, fast checks. Wording is "integrated in mission", never "merged" | stream (orchestrator/worker git activity) | `integration.merged`, `integration.conflict`, `integration.conflict_resolved`, `gate_command.run`, `gate_command.passed`, `gate_command.failed` |
| 7 | **Human** | Approvals, answers to escalations, review of the outcome (the video), the merge of the PR | app actions, stream attention events | `approval.requested`, `approval.given`, `question.answered`, `review.outcome`, `pr.merged_by_human` |
| 8 | **Outside** | The mission PR into `main`: opened, reviews, checks, attestations, merge, deploys. Empty for the observatory itself until its final PR | GitHub adapter | `pr.opened`, `pr.review_requested`, `check.started`, `check.passed`, `check.failed`, `check.required_missing`, `ruleset.blocked`, `attestation.recorded`, `attestation.verified`, `pr.merged_by_policy`, `deploy.completed` |
| 9 | **Time, Waste, Cost and models** | Tokens and usage per role, which model did what; budget meter; elapsed, stuck, and wasted time; mission overhead | derived from all lanes + session metadata | computed, not evented |

**`unknown.event`** is a first-class kind in every lane. It is counted, surfaced in an "unmapped" tray, and never dropped. M0's exit criterion is driving its count to zero on the capture.

Lane 9 is rendered as a panel that doubles as the mission's budget meter. It is the lane the other eight are measured against.

`context.compacted` is kept in lane 2 because it explains sudden quality drops in the sessions that follow it. `hook.blocked` is the write guard firing; it is counted under retry and failure.

## 11. Data sources and architecture

### 11.1 Sources

| Source | Mode | Provides |
|---|---|---|
| `~/.factory/sessions/<cwd-slug>/<session-id>.jsonl` (+ `.settings.json`), watched | **Attach (primary live mode)** | The observatory watches `~/.factory/sessions/` with a filesystem notifier, detects any new session JSONL (a mission started from any terminal on this machine), tails it as it grows and renders it in real time, named by its `--tag` or session id. Worker and validator events via the child session files. These are the canonical raw lines that lane entries link to. Read-only: no control channel. |
| Same files, finished | Replay | Same adapter: replay is attach at end-of-file, plus the time scrubber. |
| `droid exec --mission --input-format stream-jsonrpc --output-format stream-jsonrpc` | Host (secondary live mode) | Every orchestrator event; token usage; permission and question requests; the control channel (pause, message, answer). Started from the app's launch screen. |
| Git (local) | Live, polled | Mission branch, milestone worktrees, integration commits, fast-check results. |
| GitHub REST/GraphQL (user token) | Live, polled | The mission PR, reviews, check runs, required checks, rulesets, attestations, merges, deploy statuses. |
| App actions | Live | Lane 7 human events. |

Attach is primary because missions are started from the terminal in practice; the launch screen is the secondary path. Hosting is the only mode with a control channel; attach and replay are read-only views over the same files.

Open items: the exact JSON-RPC event schema for missions (how worker child sessions, feature ids, milestone ids, and validator roles are identified) is not fully documented, and where `--tag` is recorded (session settings file or first stream line) is unconfirmed. M0 captures a real mission stream, confirms both, and freezes the mapping from raw events to lane events as a versioned module with fixtures.

# droid-observatory — single source of commands.
# README, AGENTS.md, .githooks and .github/workflows all call these targets,
# so a command documented is a command CI runs (ai/RULES.md rule 5).
#
# Rust targets are no-ops until the walking skeleton lands a Cargo.toml;
# they activate automatically, nothing here needs to change.

SHELL := /bin/sh
.DEFAULT_GOAL := help

HAS_CARGO := $(wildcard Cargo.toml)
HAS_TAURI := $(wildcard apps/observatory-app/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json)
HAS_FIXTURES := $(wildcard fixtures/streams/*.jsonl)

# Thresholds (ai/RULES.md rule 4: every number has a home and a reason).
# MAX_FILE_KB: source files over this are a review smell; captured stream fixtures are exempt.
MAX_FILE_KB ?= 200

.PHONY: help doctor hooks check check-docs check-links check-workflows check-file-size \
        check-todos check-decisions-index decisions-index check-secrets \
        fmt fmt-check lint test deny replay-fixtures build app-dev app-build clean

help: ## List targets
	@grep -E '^[a-zA-Z_-]+:.*?## ' $(MAKEFILE_LIST) | awk 'BEGIN{FS=":.*?## "}{printf "  %-24s %s\n", $$1, $$2}'

doctor: ## Check local tools and print install hints
	@sh scripts/doctor.sh

hooks: ## Install git hooks (one-time after clone)
	@git config core.hooksPath .githooks && echo "hooks: core.hooksPath=.githooks"

# --- Light checks: run on every mission-branch push, must stay under 3 minutes warm ---

check: check-docs check-links check-workflows check-file-size check-todos check-decisions-index check-secrets fmt-check lint test deny replay-fixtures ## All light checks (= mission-branch CI)

check-docs: ## Lint markdown
	@markdownlint-cli2 "**/*.md"

check-links: ## Check links in markdown (needs network)
	@lychee --config lychee.toml --no-progress "**/*.md"

check-workflows: ## Lint GitHub workflows
	@actionlint

check-file-size: ## Fail on tracked files larger than MAX_FILE_KB
	@MAX_FILE_KB=$(MAX_FILE_KB) sh scripts/check-file-size.sh

check-todos: ## Debt markers must reference an issue (#123) or a backlog item (B-123)
	@sh scripts/check-todos.sh

decisions-index: ## Regenerate docs/decisions/README.md
	@sh scripts/gen-decisions-index.sh > docs/decisions/README.md

check-decisions-index: ## Fail if the decisions index is stale
	@sh scripts/gen-decisions-index.sh | diff -u docs/decisions/README.md - \
	  || { echo "decisions index stale: run 'make decisions-index'"; exit 1; }

check-secrets: ## Scan the repository for committed secrets
	@gitleaks git --no-banner --redact .

# --- Rust (active once Cargo.toml exists) ---

fmt: ## Format Rust code
ifneq (,$(HAS_CARGO))
	@cargo fmt --all
else
	@echo "fmt: no Cargo.toml yet, skipped"

#!/bin/sh
# Fails if any tracked file exceeds MAX_FILE_KB. Captured stream fixtures and the
# build log are exempt: they are data, their size is the point.
set -eu
MAX_FILE_KB=${MAX_FILE_KB:-200}
limit=$((MAX_FILE_KB * 1024))
status=0
for f in $(git ls-files); do
  case "$f" in
    fixtures/streams/*|build-log/*|Cargo.lock|*.png|*.webp|*.mp4) continue ;;
  esac
  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
  size=$(wc -c < "$f")
  if [ "$size" -gt "$limit" ]; then
    echo "too large: $f ($((size / 1024)) KB > ${MAX_FILE_KB} KB)"
    status=1
  fi
done
